messages.subject: {Disarmed} Re: [distance-sampling] Issue with dht(region.table) argument from the mrds R package
parts:
Vaughn

Specifically, the error you are encountering is caused by misconstruction of the dataframe region.table.  You have manufactured that dataframe of a single value of the region area of 155.5; hence the complaint about incorrect number of dimensions.  Help for dht describes this specification for region.table

region.table data.frame of region records. Two columns: Region.Label and Area.

Alternatively, you might investigate the R package Distance that is meant to be a simpler interface to the intricacies of the mrds package.  You should be able to use the flatfile data format, that would let you dispense with the sample.table, region.table and obs.table constructs.


On Jan 5 2019, at 7:25 pm, Vaughn Bodden <vaughn...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi all, 

This might be a basic issue but I can not get around it. Any advice would be appreciated.
I am analysing data in R using the mrds package that has no stratification by region.

Example of data head:
   Area Sample.Label   Region.Label   Effort period weather detect species size     distance
1 155.5            1                    GC               1      0           0.2      S         CP    2             0.132
2 155.5            2                    GC               1      0           0.2      H        CP     2            0.082
3 155.5            3                   GC               1       0           0.2      S        NA     NA           NA
4 155.5            4                  GC                1       0           0.0                NA     NA             NA
5 155.5            5                  GC                1       0           0.1      S        NA    NA            NA
6 155.5            6                  GC               1        0           0.1      S        CP     2              0.047

Although, the Region.Label column is included here, it has the same value "GC" for every observation.


When using the dht function, with the following code:

regionarea<- 155.5
sampleT <- parrot[,c(2,5)]

dht(parrot_model1,region.table=regionarea, sample.table=sampleT,
    se = TRUE, options = list(group=TRUE))

 I get a warning message saying :

Error in region.table[, c("Region.Label", "Area")] : 
  incorrect number of dimensions 

The dht help page says to enter a single value in the region.table argument if I have no stratification but it seems to
want the Region.Label included. I have tried fitting the model with Region.Label excluded from the data frame but
it did not change anything.I have also tried including the Region.Label with the single entry of GC for every observation
but it returns the error message: unique Region.Labels required.

I have searched online for solutions and have tried other ways of dealing with this with no success.

Any help would be great.

Thanks,
Vaughn Bodden
